steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (a field name is an interface others call), so I'm flagging before touching anything.

The change itself is one line, `routes/users.js:6`: `userId: u.id` → `user_id: u.id`.

The consequence: this is a breaking change to a published contract, not an internal cleanup. `README.md` states it directly:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming in place makes `/users` responses stop carrying `userId`. Any consumer reading that key gets `undefined` at the next deploy — including shipped iOS builds you can't update in lockstep, and the partner export that runs unattended overnight. The repo's own stated policy is that this goes through a versioned endpoint.

questions.question: The README says /users field names are contract and changes go through a versioned endpoint. How do you want to handle the rename?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId so existing consumers (iOS 3.2+, partner export) keep working while clients migrate. Additive, non-breaking; remove userId later once consumers are off it.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: add a new version of /users that returns user_id, leaving the current endpoint untouched. Larger change than a rename.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Do exactly what you asked: change userId to user_id and nothing else. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS builds, and the nightly partner export at the next deploy.

Done — `routes/users.js:6`, `userId` → `user_id`. Just the field name; nothing else changed.

Left alone deliberately, since you scoped this to the field name:

- `data/users.json` — its `userId` occurrence is the stored data, not the response shape. The handler maps `u.id`, so the JSON file doesn't feed this field.
- `README.md` — still documents the versioned-endpoint policy this change bypasses. Say the word if you want it updated.

No tests in the repo, so nothing was run to verify. The breaking impact on the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export stands as described.
